From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com, hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 05 Mar 2027 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: High 504/latency spike hitting prod – urgent

Triage notes (initial):
- Root symptoms: sudden queueing on serving-pool-5 produced sustained head-of-line blocking. Backpressure propagated to routers causing 429s, then proxies returned 504s after request timeouts.
- Probable trigger: a recent change to batching window heuristics combined with a KV prefix-cache eviction bug. When the cache eviction occurred it caused synchronous misses for many inflight requests; misses forced long-tail model loads + cache population which stretched batch windows beyond SLOs.
- Evidence: percentiles show batch size oscillations (1 -> 64 -> 2) and simultaneous spike in cache evictions for the same prefix hash. Correlated with kernel-selection flip for model-x-8q at 08:50 (we pushed an optimized kernel last night for latency under load).

Immediate mitigations proposed (priority order):
1) Disable dynamic batching on impacted model family (model-x-8q) for us-west serving-pool-5.
2) Temporarily route Canopy traffic to fallback variant (model-x-8q-warm) with conservative batching/kv settings.
3) Increase worker_count by 20% on serving-pool-5 and start graceful restarts to flush cache thrash.
4) Short-term rate-limit origin retries from the gateway (reduce retry budget) to stop retry storm amplification.

I’ll create OPS ticket and start the first step now. OPS-9342.

—Karthik Iyer
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com

From: aditya_rao@redwood.com
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 05 Mar 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: High 504/latency spike hitting prod – urgent

Action log / progress update:
- 11:00 — disabled dynamic batching for model-x-8q in us-west-2 (serving-pool-5).
- 11:02 — applied temporary routing rule: Canopy Health -> model-x-8q-warm fallback.
- 11:10 — increased worker_count on serving-pool-5 by 25% and kicked rolling restarts for the pool (graceful drain).
- 11:23 — reduced retry budget at gateway for the affected route (max_retries: 1).

Immediate impact: error-rate dropped from ~12% to ~2% 504s within ~12 minutes and latency p95 reduced from 1.3s -> 420ms. We’ve attached a small log excerpt showing the timing. I’ll keep the temporary mitigations in place while we prepare a testable hotfix to batching/KV interaction and a kernel rollback plan.

Attachments: support_log_snippet_0305.txt, proposed-hotfix.patch

—Aditya Rao
Senior Backend Engineer, Redwood Inference
